actions: Take slow breaths and say out loud what happened.
Move only far enough to escape an immediate threat such as traffic, fire, falling rock, or rising water.
Mark where you stopped and note the time, weather, and last place you were certain of your location.
cards.goal: Stop moving long enough to think clearly and avoid making the emergency larger.
cards.title: Stop and Control Panic
warnings: Do not run downhill or follow water just because it appears to lead out.

actions: Notice thirst, dry mouth, headache, dark urine, dizziness, weakness, and reduced coordination.
Rest in shade, loosen excess layers, and drink safe water in manageable amounts.
Treat confusion, collapse, seizure, or inability to drink as an emergency.
cards.goal: Reduce exertion and replace safe fluids before weakness or confusion becomes severe.
cards.title: Recognize Dehydration
warnings: Do not force fluid into anyone who is not fully alert or cannot swallow.

actions: Check wind, dryness, overhead fuel, escape routes, local restrictions, and whether a stove or insulation can meet the need.
Choose a fire only if it can remain small, attended, and fully controlled.
Prepare water, soil, or another extinguishing method before ignition.
cards.goal: Use fire only when its survival benefit exceeds wildfire, smoke, fuel, and legal risks.
cards.title: Decide Whether Fire Is Safe
warnings: Never light a fire during a ban or where wind and dry fuel can carry sparks beyond control.

actions: Move away from flood channels, unstable slopes, cliff edges, exposed ridges, roads, and avalanche paths.
Check for dead trees, hanging branches, loose rock, rising-water marks, wildlife trails, and fire spread.
Choose natural wind protection with drainage and enough visibility for signals.
cards.goal: Avoid hazards above, below, and around the site before building.
cards.title: Choose a Shelter Site
warnings: Do not choose the lowest flat ground during rain or shelter beneath a dead tree.

actions: Estimate likely rescue time, weather, health, daylight, and food already available.
Choose only methods with a high chance of return and low injury risk.
Stop if gathering consumes water, warmth, navigation certainty, or signaling time.
cards.goal: Protect warmth, water, signaling, and rescue chances before spending energy to find food.
cards.title: Decide Whether Food Gathering Is Worth It
warnings: Healthy adults can usually tolerate short food gaps better than dehydration, exposure, or injury.

actions: Stop as soon as landmarks, trail, or position stop matching expectations.
Mark the spot without damaging the environment and record time and direction of travel.
Review the last certain point, recent turns, terrain, distance, and elevation before moving.
cards.goal: Prevent the search area from growing while you reconstruct where navigation failed.
cards.title: Stop and Mark the Last Known Point
warnings: Do not keep walking simply to feel productive.

actions: Try the local emergency number; in the United States and Canada use 911 when service exists.
Give location, problem, people, injuries, supplies, weather, and planned actions.
Preserve battery, keep the device warm and dry, and follow dispatcher or beacon instructions.
cards.goal: Send a short complete rescue message whenever a phone, beacon, radio, or satellite device can connect.
cards.title: Use Emergency Communication
warnings: Do not depend on a phone alone; coverage and location reporting can fail.

actions: Check for danger before touching the person and use protective barriers when available.
Check responsiveness, open the airway as trained, and look for normal breathing and severe bleeding.
Call or send for help; begin CPR and use an AED when indicated by current training and the device prompts.
cards.goal: Make the scene safe, check responsiveness and normal breathing, and start the appropriate emergency response.
cards.title: Assess the Patient and CPR Need
warnings: Gasping is not normal breathing; do not delay emergency activation for a long examination.

actions: Leave ridges, peaks, open water, open fields, and isolated tall objects immediately.
If no safe building or vehicle exists, spread a group apart and move toward lower terrain away from water and tall isolated trees.
Wait 30 minutes after the last thunder before leaving safe shelter.
cards.goal: Reach a substantial building or hard-topped vehicle; no outdoor place is fully safe.
cards.title: Act During Lightning
warnings: A tent, cave entrance, picnic shelter, cliff overhang, or isolated tree is not reliable lightning protection.

actions: Slow smoothly, signal, and move fully out of the travel lane when the vehicle remains controllable.
Apply the parking brake, select Park or a low gear, turn on hazard lights, and assess whether staying inside is safer.
Exit away from traffic only when needed and move behind a substantial barrier when available.
cards.goal: Protect people from traffic, fire, slope, and weather before diagnosing the vehicle.
cards.title: Stop and Secure the Scene
warnings: Never work in a live traffic lane; move well away from smoke, fire, fuel smell, or a damaged high-voltage battery.
